title: A $700 Emergency Can Cost You $999. Here's the Fix
summary: Maya and Jordan get the same $700 surprise bill in the same week. Maya pays it from savings; Jordan puts it on a credit card and, paying $25 a month, ends up paying about $999 over 40 months. This video explains the emergency fund: why surprise bills are a when and not an if, a $1,000 starter fund, then 3 to 6 months of essential costs, where the money should live (a separate insured savings account), why it does not belong in the stock market, what counts as an emergency, and the honest cost of keeping cash. The card example assumes the Fed's August 2026 average rate of 22.36% on accounts assessed interest; budgets and bills are made-up examples, savings rates change often, and the 7% investment return is an example, not a prediction. Maya and Jordan are fictional composites.
